item.description:
NVBeacon is a native macOS menu bar app for monitoring remote NVIDIA GPU servers over SSH with `nvidia-smi`, process exit alerts, and GPU idle notifications.
- Added per-server network usage: download and upload rates plus total transferred bytes, shown in the popover and in the menu bar tooltip. - Read network interface counters (`/sys/class/net`, falling back to `/proc/net/dev`) inside the existing polling SSH call, skipping loopback, container, and overlay interfaces as well as bond/bridge slaves. - Grouped CPU, RAM/Swap, and network metrics in one host information section, expanded by default, with a saved expand/collapse state per server. - Added collapsible server cards, expanded by default, with saved states independent of each server's host information section. Collapsing either section keeps polling and alerts running. - Unified GPU and host query editors as matching single-line fields, preserving multiline script behavior through an executable single-line representation. - Replaced the per-server memory-only command editor with a complete host information script for CPU, RAM/Swap, and network collection; preserved existing custom memory queries through migration. Server backup v2 preserves host scripts and still imports v1 backups. - Added host information collection controls in General settings: turn all collection off or select CPU, memory, and network individually. Individual switches are hidden while collection is off, with their choices retained. The default host script skips disabled probes. - Hid unconfigured swap and moved available RAM into the RAM bar tooltip to keep host information compact. - Calculated CPU utilization between regular polls, removing the extra 0.2-second sampling delay while keeping a single SSH query for GPU and host metrics. - Suppressed network rates for samples less than one second apart, and retained bond/bridge slave filtering when falling back to `/proc/net/dev` with available interface topology. - Added a one-time Mac-to-iPhone server transfer in Advanced settings, with QR pairing, a six-digit comparison code, Touch ID or Mac password approval, and an encrypted local-network connection. Transferring needs the iOS app, which is still in the works and not on the App Store yet. - Changed server export to record each target's effective username, hostname, and port, so backups no longer depend on local SSH aliases. Export now stops without writing a partial backup when a target requires ProxyJump or ProxyCommand. Normal monitoring still uses the saved SSH target. - Thanks @JunbiaoXue for contributing server network and CPU monitoring in #7.
